claim.why_it_matters: The figure was reduced to a scatter of its text labels (legend entries interleaved with box labels, the arrow captions turned into a two-row table). The nesting that the figure exists to show (which source elements sit in which source unit, and how compilation units map onto runtime modules in a run unit) and the legend's border-style key are lost. Annex E is informative, so no normative rule is affected.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page 745 (printed p. 723) shows Figure E.3 as a box diagram. The markdown holds only its text labels, scrambled: the legend entries are interleaved with the P-1 box labels, and the four arrow captions became a meaningless two-row table. The nesting, the arrows (including the unlabelled arrow from the middle compilation unit to the middle runtime module), and the legend's border-style key are all lost. The intro sentence and the caption are present. The claim's description of the nesting is slightly wrong, though. In the printed figure, P-1-1, P-1-2, P-1-2-1 and P-1-2-2 are drawn with thin solid borders, which the legend assigns to Source Unit, and each holds a dashed Source Element box. P-1 also holds its own dashed source element across the top. Annex E is informative, so no normative rule is affected.
verdict.corrected_description: Figure E.3 is reduced to scrambled text labels. Printed figure: a thick-bordered compilation group holds three compilation units (thin double-line boxes). The middle unit holds source unit P-1, which has its own dashed source element and the nested source units P-1-1 and P-1-2. P-1-2 in turn holds the nested source units P-1-2-1 and P-1-2-2. Each source unit has a dashed source element. Arrows labelled 'To other run unit' lead down from the outer compilation units. A bracketed arrow leads from the middle compilation unit to the middle runtime module. Arrows labelled 'From other comp. group' lead into the outer runtime modules. The thick-bordered run unit below holds three runtime modules, and the middle one carries dashed runtime elements that mirror the source elements. A legend maps the border styles to Compilation Group, Compilation Unit, Source Unit, Source Element, Run Unit, Runtime Module and Runtime Element. All of the structure and the legend key are lost. This is informative Annex E, so it has no normative impact.
